# DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#dsabench)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14700v1) · arXiv:2610.14700v1, 10 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 39 pages: sections 1–8, use/ethics/reproducibility statements, references and Appendices A–L including every task card, prompt, metric definition and numeric table. All four figures visually inspected.

## Research question

Selecting a plausible database does not ensure that all required sources, cross-database dependencies and executable local contributions have been recovered.

## Method

DSABench composes executable source units into hidden contracts, then renders and reviews requests. RouteEnv exposes catalog evidence through opaque source identifiers. Scores separate exact source recovery, topology/dependencies, local execution and their conjunction; interactive tasks use two equally weighted latent branches.

## Evaluation

The 815 tasks include 618 jointly multi-source and 105 interactive tasks, but only 22 sequential dependencies. Seven backends support a routing study; four support a 72-configuration factorial study. Clarification is evaluated through a one-question semantic-slot simulator.

## What the results support

Clarification improves exact branch-source recovery by about 40–43 points. Router-local requests improve individual source execution but do not consistently improve complete workflow success. The best non-privileged clarified conjunction is 16.99%, selected descriptively from the evaluated grid.

## Limits and qualifications

RA-Graph includes a behavior-label gate, and Never Ask’s zero interactive conjunction is partly due to that gate, not universal SQL failure. Preserved examples omit gold constraints from visible wording. Review agreement cannot be reconstructed; evidence/compute schedules differ, and corpus-specific comparators differ. The workflow score does not evaluate final prose answers or unrestricted dialogue.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for studying ambiguity that changes which database should be queried, and for separating source-set errors, information transfer and local-query failures while preserving benchmark validity boundaries.
